'''Peter Watts''' (born January 25, 1958<ref name="isfdb"/>) is a Canadian [[science fiction]] author.  He specializes in [[hard science fiction]].  He earned a Ph.D. from the [[University of British Columbia]] in 1991 from the Department of Zoology and Resource Ecology.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Watts |first=Peter |date=1991 |title=Hauling Out Behaviour of Harbour Seals |url=https://open.library.ubc.ca/media/download/pdf/831/1.0302424/1 |journal=University of British Columbia}}</ref> He went on to hold several academic research and teaching positions, and worked as a marine-mammal biologist.  He began publishing fiction around the time he finished graduate school.

==Career==
His first novel ''Starfish'' (1999) reintroduced Lenie Clarke from his short story "A Niche" (1990); Clarke is a deep-ocean [[power station]] worker physically altered for underwater living and the main character in the sequels: ''Maelstrom'' (2001), ''βehemoth: β-Max'' (2004) and ''βehemoth: Seppuku'' (2005). The last two volumes constitute one novel, but were published separately for commercial reasons.<ref name="nyt1"/> ''Starfish'', ''Maelstrom'', and ''βehemoth'' make up a trilogy usually referred to as "Rifters" after the modified humans designed to work in deep-ocean environments.

His novel ''[[Blindsight (science fiction novel)|Blindsight]]'', released in October 2006, was nominated for a [[Hugo Award for Best Novel|Hugo Award]]. The novel was described by [[Charles Stross]]: "Imagine a neurobiology-obsessed version of [[Greg Egan]] writing a first contact with aliens story from the point of view of a zombie posthuman crewman aboard a starship captained by a vampire, with not dying as the booby prize."<ref name="nicoll"/>  ''[[Echopraxia (novel)|Echopraxia]]'' (2014) is a "sidequel" about events happening on Earth and elsewhere concurrent with the events in ''Blindsight''.<ref name="echopraxia-tor-review"/>

Watts has made some of his novels and short fiction available on his website under a [[Creative Commons]] license. He believes that doing so has "actually ''saved'' [his] career outright, by rescuing ''Blindsight'' from the oblivion to which it would have otherwise been doomed.<ref name="pw213"/> The week after [he] started giving ''Blindsight'' away, sales tripled."<ref name="reddit-ama"/>

In addition to writing novels and short stories, Watts has also worked in other media. He was peripherally involved in the early stages of the animated science fiction film and television project ''[[Strange Frame]]''.<ref name="strange-frame"/> He also worked briefly with [[Relic Entertainment]] on one of the early drafts of the story that would eventually, years later, become ''[[Homeworld 2]]''. However, the draft Watts worked on bears no resemblance to the one used for the released game.<ref name="reddit-ama"/> More recently, he has been recruited<ref name="pw557"/> by [[Crytek]] as a writer and art consultant on ''[[Crysis 2]]''. Technological elements from ''Blindsight'' have been referenced in the fictional ''Crysis 2'' "Nanosuit Brochure";<ref name="crynet"/> the creative director of ''[[BioShock 2]]'' has cited Watts's work as an influence on that game.<ref name="biosh"/>
[[File:Peter Watts in Helsinki 2013 C IMG 4148.JPG|thumb|Watts at Finncon 2013 in [[Helsinki]], Finland]]

==Personal life==

In December 2009, Watts was detained at the [[Canada–United States border]] by [[U.S. Customs and Border Protection]] (CBP) to perform a reportedly random search of the rental vehicle he was driving. Watts is alleged to have assaulted a CBP Officer and was turned over to local authorities to face charges. According to an officer, the authorities used [[pepper spray]] to subdue Watts after Watts became aggressive toward officers.<ref name="star2"/> According to Watts, he was assaulted, punched in the face, pepper-sprayed, and thrown in jail for the night.<ref name="pw932"/> The officer later admitted in court that he had punched Watts. A jury found Watts guilty of obstructing a U.S. Customs and Border Protection officer. He faced a maximum sentence of 2 years in prison. Watts blogged about his sentence saying that because of how the law was written, his asking, "What is the problem?", was enough to convict him of non-compliance.<ref name="jury"/> In April 2010, he was given a suspended sentence and a fine.<ref name="fine">{{cite web |first=David |last=Nickle |work=The Devil's Exercise Yard |title=Peter Watts is Free |url=https://davidnickle.blogspot.com/2010/04/peter-watts-is-free.html |date=26 April 2010}}</ref> However, due to immigration laws,<ref name="thelaw">{{cite web |website=trac.syr.edu|publisher=[[Transactional Records Access Clearinghouse]] |title=Aggravated Felonies and Deportation |url=http://trac.syr.edu/immigration/reports/155/ |year=2006}}</ref> Watts' felony conviction prevents him from re-entering the United States.<ref name="overseas">{{cite web |first=Madeline |last=Ashby |website=Tor.com |title=Sometimes, we win. |url=http://www.tor.com/2010/04/27/sometimes-we-win/ |date=27 April 2010}}</ref>

In February 2011, Watts contracted the rare disease [[necrotizing fasciitis]] in his leg, which he has blogged about on his website.<ref>{{cite web|last=Watts|first=Peter|title=Flesh Eating Fest '11|url=http://www.rifters.com/crawl/?category_name=flesh-eating-fest-11|website=Rifters.com}}</ref>

He married fellow Canadian author [[Caitlin Sweet]] in August 2011.<ref name="Watts"/>

*"The Island" (''[[The New Space Opera 2]]'', 2009)
*"Hotshot" (''[[Reach for Infinity]]'', 2014)<ref name="Tor Infinity">{{cite web |url=http://www.tor.com/2014/06/12/book-review-anthology-reach-for-infinity-jonathan-strahan/ |title=Step into the Stars: ''Reach for Infinity'', ed. *"Hitchhiker" (2018, story fragment, published online. Link was in ''The Freeze-Frame Revolution'')<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://rifters.com/Eriophora-Root-Archive-Log-Ahzmundin--frag/derelict.htm|title=Araneus|website=rifters.com|access-date=2019-11-21}}</ref>

*"Periscope Depth" (2026, story fragment, published online. Available through Watt's blog.)<ref name="Periscope Depth" />

The chronological order within the Sunflower universe is: "Hotshot", ''The Freeze-Frame Revolution'', "Giants", "Hitchhiker", "Strategic Retreat", "Remora", "Outtake", "The Island".
